transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul has appointed Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor in the alleged gang rape at Cornell University Fraternity House in 2024.
In a statement, Hochul said she is turning to James, the state attorney general, because she has lost faith in local district attorney Matthew Van Houten's ability to handle the case.
Van Houten is facing criticism that he abandoned the initial investigation too quickly.
NPR's Brian Mann is at Cornell and has more on what Van Houten is saying.
Van Houten has now suggested in a statement that Cornell campus police didn't give him all the necessary information from their interviews with the woman.
He says he never saw that statement, that she was 100% confident that she was raped.
Here's what Van Houten said in an email to our member station WSKG.
If it's factual, he wrote, we absolutely should have been informed about what Jane Doe said to the police.
That was not in her six-page statement.
Attorneys for Tennessee death row inmate Krista Pike say Pike is still alive but in critical condition after the state's failed attempt to execute Pike by lethal injection.
From member station WPLM, Mariana Bacchiao reports on Tennessee Republican Governor Bill Lee's call for a third-party review of what went wrong.
This marks the second time Governor Bill Lee has issued a moratorium to review the state's execution protocols.
A 2022 review found that the drugs used had not been properly inspected, leading to an overhaul of the system and a new lethal injection process.
This is a process that has been used over 100 times in this country without this outcome.
Lee is term limited and will likely not be governor when the investigation is complete. The front-runner for the governorship, U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn, has called for the state to "bring back the electric chair."
For NPR News, I'm Mariana Bacchiao in Nashville.
Now that it's October, refugees and other groups of immigrants with legal status are losing Medicaid coverage.
NPR's Selina Simmons-Duffin reports a change as a result of Republicans' One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Mustafa Rifat has lately been fielding frantic phone calls from refugees with disabilities.
It's a nightmare for the community.
It's a very emotional time because they also lost their access to food stamps.
Rifat is a professor of social work at the University of Nebraska at Omaha and a former refugee himself.
He points out these are new Americans who are often struggling with complex health issues while adjusting to a new culture.
Making their health and well-being worse is not going to benefit anyone.
In a statement to NPR, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services emphasized it is implementing a law passed by Congress.
Selina Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
This is NPR. Rescue teams in Southern California are looking for a fifth person who remains missing following the crash of a medical helicopter Wednesday off California's Catalina Island.
The Coast Guard says the helicopter was transporting a patient off the island when it went down shortly after takeoff.
Two people were killed and two others were hospitalized.
The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating.
Mortgage rates are at their highest level in almost three years.
The average 30-year fixed rate mortgage, now almost 7.3%, NPR's Stephen Pissaha reports.
Mortgage interest rates often go up with the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, and that yield has been floating around a more than two decade high.
Mortgage rates are up a quarter of a percent from last week.
John Diamond is an economist at Rice University, and he says the high cost of borrowing is having a bad lock-in effect on the economy.
People are staying put. That's going to slow down consumption growth, but hopefully that will eventually lead to lower inflation.
The Federal Reserve will consider raising interest rates again later this month to fight inflation.
Stephen Pissaha, NPR News.
A quick flight to the International Space Station. Four astronauts have arrived at the orbiting outpost following an eight-hour flight.
That's a fastest journey to the station for not only SpaceX, but any other U.S. entity, including NASA.
Among the four, Commander Jessica Watkins, she is the first black woman to lead a crew to orbit.
They are to spend six months aboard the station. This is NPR.
Stay tuned for the following announcements and messages from our sponsors.

topics.text: New York Governor Hochul appoints Attorney General James as special prosecutor in Cornell University alleged gang rape case
Tennessee death row inmate Krista Pike remains alive in critical condition after failed lethal injection execution
Governor Bill Lee calls for third-party review of Tennessee's failed execution and lethal injection protocols
Refugees and legal immigrants losing Medicaid coverage in October due to Republican legislative changes
Rescue teams search for fifth missing person after medical helicopter crash off California's Catalina Island
Mortgage rates reach highest level in almost three years at 7.3 percent
Four astronauts including Commander Jessica Watkins arrive at International Space Station after eight-hour SpaceX flight
